item.title: Security — the trust model and the security document
item.description: Who and what Moonkale trusts on each platform, and the skeleton of the project's security document. It covers secrets, connections, prompt injection, untrusted content and exploits, extensions, the supply chain and data at rest, plus the rules every change follows so security issues don't pile up. What is enforced where today, and the open findings.

item.title: Work Packages
item.description: The open work cut into packages that several agents can carry at once without colliding — each with its files, dependencies, size and acceptance — plus the rules that keep parallel branches mergeable. Drafted 2026-10-14 for a multi-agent setup.

item.title: Code Graph Schema — definitions, identity and edges for many languages on one graph
item.description: Draft spec (2026-10-15) for the North Star's code graph: what a definition is in each language, the two ids (where it is, and what it is: a content hash of its normalised structure), names as edges, the edge kinds code needs, layers from text to IR, and provenance on everything derived. Rust, Julia and Python are worked out as the first cases; a Unison codebase (WP-18) checks the model. ADR-0028 (accepted: B) lets graph views edit file-backed code through text patches.

item.title: Moonkale — Vault Home
item.description: Moonkale is a graph-native code and knowledge editor: it opens folders and database connections, shows everything as one graph, and is driven by extensions.

item.title: Recoco and Thread — requirements and fit for Moonkale
item.description: What two neighbouring code-intelligence projects require and propose, how that fits Moonkale, and whether it would help, as requirements prior art only (Thread is AGPL-licensed, so no code is reused).
